newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt Sept passenger traffic dips 0.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt Sept passenger traffic dips 0.4 pct.

text.p: Passenger numbers at Frankfurt Airport fell 0.4 percent in September due to weak demand caused by weak economic activity, airport authority Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG) said.
A total of 3.76 million passengers flew from Frankfurt last month, the FAG market research department said in its latest monthly report.
Passenger numbers are showing a January-September rise of 1.6 percent to 29.46 million, the report added.
"The weak economic situation still showed its effect. Domestic traffic is developing negatively," the report said.
"Private travel by Germans is showing signs of weakness. Seemingly the rising (financial) impact on private households is increasingly having a negative effect on demand," it added.
Additional traffic gained last summer by the partial closing of Stuttgart Airport had also been lost, the report noted.
The number of aircraft movements declined 0.8 percent in September as several routes were cut on grounds of viability.
But the average number of passengers per flight rose slightly to 112.7 to reach a new monthly record, the report said.
